corrections.value: Releases the Proteus-2k evaluation dataset and introduces an algorithm that recovers near-full-data frontiers using roughly 20% of the evaluation budget.

The abstract identifies terminal binary feedback and describes interpolation from expected-reward RL toward maximum likelihood as sampling compute increases, but does not give the precise objective formula or full proof assumptions.
A closed-form intrinsic-noise characterization enables stable privacy-utility trade-offs through bounded, gauge-invariant perturbations.
The abstract pairs a systems bottleneck with a mechanism tailored to sparse, dynamically changing pixel influence, then reports a quality comparison at different GPU and Gaussian counts.

The abstract connects joint graph-and-feature intervention to spectral-space alignment, states applicability to differing homophily or heterophily levels, and separately reports broad synthetic and real-world comparisons.

Assuming first-order oracle cost N and second-order oracle cost dN, the authors report Õ((N+d²)(d+d^(2/3)ε^(-2/3))) for convex-concave problems and Õ((N+d²)(d+d^(2/3)κ^(2/3))) for strongly-convex-strongly-concave problems with condition number κ.

The abstract lists factor generation, coarse probability estimation, and relevance assessment as useful LLM capabilities, then proposes a Bayesian-network framework using LLM abductions followed by deduction.

From a biological simulation examining selected genes from over 11,000 candidates, the authors suggest that the generated network has potential to identify subtype-specific genes with an 83% likelihood of impacting patient-distribution shifts; the likelihood's operational definition is unspecified.
Multimodal image fusion and object detection are important for autonomous driving.
The abstract states that CTD has the same reported p-Wasserstein convergence bounds as NTD, but does not detail the assumptions or derivation needed to obtain them.

The abstract links reconstruction-induced value discrepancy to optimization errors, proposes a one-to-one normalizing-flow mapping to eliminate that gap, and additionally introduces importance-adaptive token sampling without specifying its relationship to gap repair.

Given a dataset, the abstract describes a polynomial-time check of whether all best-fit multi-head linear-attention networks perform an identical computation, and connects this property to out-of-distribution generalization.
This approach may be unsuitable when the relevant model class is misspecified or when its best-fit solution set cannot be characterized by a tractable check.

The abstract specifies that the evaluation protocol quantifies online tuning budgets, but does not give the detailed protocol, statistical treatment, or conditions underlying the reported performance gains.
No quantitative metrics, dataset names, baselines beyond Label Smoothing, or experimental conditions are provided.
The abstract states that anonymous code was submitted for future public release, and also states that code is available at the supplied repository URL.
The abstract explicitly contrasts binary usage inference with proportion-level estimation and pairs the proposed method with a reported maximum error and a computational-cost comparison.
The abstract does not specify the remaining model's outcome or whether the reported results generalize beyond the named datasets and open-weight models.

The abstract identifies a potentially suboptimal estimated loss introduced by directly adapting LLM preference methods, then proposes score matching to align diffusion pretraining and fine-tuning objectives.

The abstract motivates TI-DPO with noise sensitivity and inadequate token-importance modeling, then assigns complementary roles to hybrid weighting for accurate, robust importance scores and triplet loss for preferred-versus-non-preferred output guidance.

The authors present MedAgentGym as an integrated platform with a unified execution environment, a comprehensive benchmark, and accessible, extensible training resources for biomedical coding assistants.
The authors position Med-Copilot, trained using MedAgentGym, as a cost-effective, privacy-preserving alternative competitive with gpt-4o.
Existing methods use strong structural assumptions, while a general approach without structural assumptions lacks an equivalence characterization needed to determine what is identifiable.
The authors identify missing equivalence characterization as an obstacle to methods without structural assumptions and address this gap for linear non-Gaussian models.
Reports qualitative estimates derived from the bounds, empirical verification of their insights, and a sharper account of extrapolation mechanisms.

The abstract states a common simulation condition spanning distinct error, precision, and depth settings, while separately reporting qualitative estimates derived from its bounds and empirical verification of the insights.

S5 lacks the numbering marker (2), but includes an intervening observation about design choices primarily affecting compute efficiency; the supplied abstract does not establish whether any substantive content is missing.

S8–S9 jointly report win-rate increases for weaker LMs such as Llama-4-Scout from 8% to 82% against humans and from 0% to 67% against GPT-5, at approximately 1% of GPT-5's cost; detailed comparison protocols and the cost calculation are not specified in the abstract.
The abstract reports identifying three atomic capabilities in visual verification and states that they generalize and interact synergistically, without naming the capabilities.

The abstract names LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2.5-VL but does not provide the complete roster of three evaluated VLLMs, the identities of the five benchmarks, baseline methods, or detailed evaluation protocols.

It combines dual-mode pre-training with cross-mode post-training distillation that matches the consistent 3D-oriented mode's distribution to the high-quality MV-oriented mode's distribution, aiming to improve 3D-oriented visual quality while maintaining 3D consistency.

The abstract presents space-time separation, random features in place of gradient-descent training, and built-in temporal causality in response to optimization and non-causal time-treatment bottlenecks, then reports overall performance across nine PDE benchmarks with varied challenges.

The authors report that their analysis indicates the mitigations substantially increase attack cost; Cloudflare bot protection, malicious-user detection, and rate limiting predated the collaboration, while reCAPTCHA and login were being integrated.

The authors collaborated with Chatbot Arena developers to identify, propose, and implement mitigations; Cloudflare bot protection, malicious-user detection, and rate limiting were already present before the collaboration, while reCAPTCHA and login were being integrated.
Sonnet 3.5 and Opus 4 have similar reported attack success on CTF-like defenses (75% and 79%), but a wider separation on real-world defenses (13% and 30%).

The authors describe arbitrary-length time-series conditioning, pre-training without specifying a prior distribution, and generation of multiple probable predictions with greater representational flexibility than parametric densities.

The authors report a representational merger effect and interpret it as finite-automaton construction; the abstract does not clarify whether that correspondence is formally proved or empirically inferred.
The authors report improving Qwen2.5-Math-7B on MATH from 58.8% to 90.0%, surpassing o1-preview by a stated +4.5%, whose relative-versus-percentage-point interpretation is unspecified.
The authors report solving an average of 53.3% (8/15) of AIME problems and describe this as among the top 20% of the brightest high-school math students; the comparison basis is unspecified.
The authors report that XR-1 consistently outperforms π_0 and GR00T-N1.5, while generalizing to novel objects, backgrounds, distractors, and illumination changes.

The authors report complementary experiments on 31 tasks spanning online and offline RL: stronger performance with more compute and stronger generalization on longer-horizon test tasks compared with standard feedforward networks or deep residual networks using up to five times more parameters.

The authors bound optimal-policy sensitivity by the ratio of the Q-function's mixed-partial derivative (described as noise sensitivity) to its action-space curvature (described as signal distinctness), and describe PAVE as minimizing Q-gradient volatility while preserving local curvature.

The abstract reports five optimization dimensions spanning agent functionality and collaboration structure, without enumerating them, then describes separate single-dimension and joint-optimization algorithms.
Introduces piecewise-linear convex pricing and reports existence of a pricing profile in which no seller can improve revenue by a factor of two by deviating to any uniform price.
Simulations reportedly converge quickly and achieve empirical approximation guarantees better than the worst-case factor of 2.
The abstract identifies that 1-WL can count homomorphisms of trees, while the proposed extension counts cactus-graph homomorphisms.
The authors describe r-ℓWL as a novel hierarchy and position it as extending 1-WL.
Frames the cactus-homomorphism result as extending 1-WL, which is described as limited to tree homomorphisms.

corrections.value: For discounted MDPs, the authors report bounds Õ(SA H/((1−γ)²ε²)) for weakly communicating instances and Õ(SA(B+H)/((1−γ)²ε²)) for general instances, yielding quadratic horizon dependence for a fixed MDP instance rather than contradicting the general cubic minimax lower bound.
The authors report cross-model 3H improvements, including average gains for Aligner-7B; separately, a community report describes a leaderboard gain from stacking Aligner-2B on GPT-4 Turbo.
In Football, the authors report that URI beat built-in AIs with a reported 37%, without explicitly naming that percentage's metric; a GPT-based agent achieved a 6% winning rate.
The authors construct Tic-Tac-Toe and Football benchmarks and report at least a 44% net win rate against GPT-based agents without real data, followed by a separate Football comparison.

The authors state that their evaluation of 43 language models establishes two dominant response patterns: ordering and labeling biases, and a trend toward uniformly random survey responses after randomized answer ordering.
The authors report that, after randomized answer ordering, the evaluated models trend toward uniformly random survey responses, irrespective of model size or training data within the evaluated set.

The abstract reports ordering and labeling biases, followed by a trend toward uniformly random survey responses among evaluated models after randomized answer ordering, potentially misleading conclusions about model alignment.
The abstract does not report uncertainty estimates, statistical tests, or the precise basis for the reported trend toward uniformly random survey responses.

The abstract names audio synchronization, facial nuances, and natural head motions as capabilities contributing to perceived authenticity and liveliness, and separately reports experiments using unspecified new metrics and improvements across unspecified dimensions.

The authors report significant improvements over state-of-the-art models across various metrics on a publicly available fMRI-video dataset, including a 128% improvement in SSIM and an 81% improvement in unspecified spatiotemporal metrics.

The abstract connects expanded Earth-system variables to boundary conditions and physics-based metrics to physical consistency and the butterfly effect; it also includes forecasts from four national weather agencies, addressing the separately stated gap in operational baseline coverage.
The abstract identifies disrupted continuity at clip boundaries and introduces modules combining semantic guidance with phase details from adjacent clips in a transition-aware representation.

The abstract links a calibration guarantee to a regret guarantee and separately gives a lower bound showing that exponential dependence on inverse accuracy is necessary in the stated simplex regime; it does not establish matching rates.

The abstract states inverse-model-dimension scaling but does not provide fitted exponent estimates or uncertainties, model dimensions, datasets, or details of the reported confirmation in open-sourced LLMs.
